ai_summary.headline: Cash is almost absent from Chad's plan: MPCA is 0.2% of requirements and shows no funding in FTS.
ai_summary.narrative: The 2026 HNRP asks for USD 986M and is about 45% funded, but most of that sits in the refugee response [s2][s3]. MPCA is the only separately costed cash line at USD 1.82M, 0.18% of the plan, after a 2025 MPCA component of USD 5.7M received nothing; the target fell from 104,800 to 33,444 people [s1]. FTS shows no funding to the MPC cluster [s3]. Yet H1 2025 reporting cited 46 partners delivering about USD 11.4M in cash to 228,230 people, which suggests the plan understates real cash activity [s1]. The sharpest recent signal is the USD 100M US-OCHA allocation, of which USD 18.8M is cash and USD 4.5M MPCA, now being assessed by CALP with the CWG [s5][s6]. The CWG is government-led with a leadership handover to MASSAH under way, and reports declining funding as its main challenge [s4]. There appears to be little recent evidence on modality preference, cost efficiency or markets.
barriers: MPCA unfunded in 2025 and no funding visible in FTS for 2026 [s3]
No aggregated CVA figure in the HNRP, so cash is hard to track [s1]
CWG leadership transition to government not complete [s4]
No modality preference or cost-efficiency data found
opportunities: The CALP and CWG assessment of the USD 100M allocation can inform the next pooled allocation [s5]
Large sectoral cash footprint (food security USD 18 per person per month) could anchor a consolidated CVA figure [s1]
data_gaps: Plan document not independently opened (figures via gDCF analysis)
